# vita-memio 1.5.0

This release **fixes several rare but serious bugs** from 1.4.0, so please update. It also makes *Adaptive* remember what it learned for every game across restarts and switch read ahead off where it does not pay off. Learned data and game profiles move off the internal storage to `ux0:data/vita-memio/`.

**Everything is now in one archive, `vita-memio-1.5.0.zip`.** Unpack it and copy the three plugin files as before; see *Install or update* below.

## Fixed

- **Old data after a write (very small reads).** A write could, rarely, fail to drop the block of very small reads it changed, and the next read could get the data from before the write. This is the most important fix in this release.
- **Another game's settings.** When two apps started at the same moment, a game could get the other app's title, and with it its profile, its learned read ahead and its overlay *Save*.
- **HUD crash.** The HUD could read past its buffer if it was drawn just as its picture was being replaced.
- **HUD of another version.** If `vitamemio_hud.skprx` did not match the other files, it stayed hooked into the system with nothing to stop it. Now it is unloaded and the HUD stays off until all three files are updated together.
- **Waits when a game saves.** Read ahead read a piece while a write was running and then threw it away, so the game's reads waited behind it for nothing. Now that piece is skipped and read ahead goes on after the write.

## New

- **Adaptive remembers every game, also across restarts.** In 1.4.0 it kept what it learned for the last eight games until the console restarted. Now each game comes back where it left off, from `ux0:data/vita-memio/tuning.bin` (about 370 bytes per game, written only when something changed).
- **Adaptive switches read ahead off where it costs time.** It counts what read ahead actually saved in each game, separately for ordinary memory, graphics memory and very small reads. Where that comes out as a loss, read ahead goes off for that kind of read, and comes back on when the game's own figures show a gain. The HUD shows `-` for a kind that is off.
- **Driver** (Settings, on by default): whether the plugin starts with the console. Off: from the next start it loads nothing, and the Settings page stays so you can switch it back on.
- **Profiles for system apps** (Advanced, on by default): the home screen and the system's own apps get their own settings in the overlay and their own learning, like games.
- **Log:** with *Enable log* on, each app leaving the front writes a summary of its reads: how long they took by size, what read ahead served, wasted and skipped, and Adaptive's changes.

## Changed

- **Nothing happens while the console starts.** The plugin sets aside its memory, but every transfer goes the standard way until the home screen is up. The boot guard no longer depends on timers: a start counts as good once the plugin's first 64 transfers have worked.
- **Fewer writes to the internal storage.** Game profiles (`ra/`) and `tuning.bin` are now on `ux0:data/vita-memio/`. Files from 1.4.0 on `ur0:` are moved there automatically, and the measured *Tuning* figures are kept. A profile is written in place, only when it changes, and is no longer deleted when you set it back to the defaults.

## Results in games

These are the plugin's own estimates from its log (PCH-1000, microSD in an SD2Vita), from one short session per game with loading screens. *Saved* is the time read ahead took off the game's waits for the card. They are rough figures, not stopwatch measurements.

| Game | Session | Reads took | Saved by read ahead |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PCSG01179 | 174 s | 9.4 s | 52.8 s (85%) |
| GTA San Andreas (port) | 87 s | 15.1 s | 22.5 s (60%) |
| PCSB00404 | 28 s | 2.8 s | 12.4 s (81%) |
| NFS Underground 2 (port) | 104 s | 11.7 s | 12.0 s (51%) |
| PCSB00419 | 82 s | 3.0 s | 2.0 s (40%) |
| PCSB00986 | 90 s | 2.9 s | 1.6 s (35%) |
| PCSE01254 | 134 s | 8.2 s | 1.5 s (16%) |
| PCSB00554 | 95 s | 4.7 s | 1.5 s (24%) |
| PCSB01030 | 104 s | 10.2 s | 1.1 s (10%) |
| PCSB00296 | 78 s | 5.8 s | 1.0 s (15%) |
| PCSF00024 | 167 s | 32.1 s | 0.8 s (2%) |
| PCSB00245 | 64 s | 2.1 s | 0.7 s (24%) |
| PCSB00724 | 67 s | 3.4 s | 0.3 s (8%) |
| PCSB00118 | 222 s | 6.0 s | 0.3 s (4%) |

In PCSE01254, which saves often, the skipped pieces brought the gain from 0.8 s to 1.5 s. No game waited behind read ahead for longer than 17 ms at a time.

## Good to know

- Tested on one console: a PCH-1000 on firmware 3.65.
- Settings from 1.4.0 are kept.
- If you see error **C1-2569-2** (out of kernel memory), see the [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#error-c1-2569-2).

## Install or update

Unpack `vita-memio-1.5.0.zip`. Copy `vitamemio_kernel.skprx`, `vitamemio_hud.skprx` and `vitamemio.suprx` to `ur0:tai/` and restart; always update all three together. `vitamemio_hud.skprx` does not go in `config.txt`. `vitamemio_tester.vpk` is the optional tester, and `SHA256SUMS` lets you check the files. For a new install, add the plugin's lines to `config.txt` first; see the [README](https://github.com/Osaul4ik/vita-memio#install).

To uninstall: switch off every storage (or *Driver*), remove the plugin's lines from `config.txt`, restart, then delete the three files and the folders `ur0:data/vita-memio/` and `ux0:data/vita-memio/`.
